title: AuroraCloud - Redwood marketplace/reference arch/joint solution sync
next_steps: Jordan to share Redwood marketplace listing checklist and draft copy (includes pricing and SKU suggestions)
Priya to upload reference architecture diagram and sample terraform snippets to partner repo
AuroraCloud to complete partner security questionnaire and provide SOC2 summary
action_items: Jordan Lee: Send marketplace listing checklist and sample RA by 2026-05-18
Priya Nair: Provide integration diagram, terraform snippets, and latency benchmark spreadsheet by 2026-05-20
Marta Ruiz: Share partner security questionnaire responses and contact for legal review by 2026-05-22
summary: Partner technical sync to align marketplace listing requirements, finalize a reference architecture for Redwood-in-AuroraCloud joint solution, and agree on next steps for a joint marketplace listing pilot. Discussed listing metadata, billing/SKU model, network diagrams (VPC peering vs private link), KMS/HSM requirements, SOC2 artifacts, and a lightweight latency benchmark plan. Decided to run a small joint pilot and exchange artifacts to prep the marketplace submission and reference arch doc.
topics: reference architecture for private deployments/VPC options
transcript:
00:00 Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the AuroraCloud partnership. we've got priya, our se, and carlos taking notes. is the time still good?
00:06 Marta (AuroraCloud): Yep, good for us, thanks jordan.
00:12 Priya (Redwood SE): quick intro from me, i'll focus on the reference arch and the integration points for the marketplace package.
00:18 Samir (AuroraCloud): great, i'll be looking at the networking and infra bits, V P C, private link, things like that.
00:26 Jordan: high-level agenda, marketplace listing fields, reference arch, security/compliance checklist, and a small pilot for latency/cost bench. ok?
00:33 Leah (AuroraCloud): yep also curious about billing SKUs and whether customers will be billed via Redwood or via Aurora marketplace.
00:40 Jordan: good question. so we usually support two modes: hosted API via Redwood (we bill) or marketplace listing where partner resells and does consolidated billing. we can do listing metadata either as direct redirect to our hosted plan or as a joint SKU where AuroraCloud lists a managed offer.
00:58 Priya: technically the integration is straightforward for the hosted redirect — simple link and API keys. for the dedicated/private deployment listing we need a reference arch doc: networking, IAM, KMS keys, and expected perf.
01:10 Samir: on networking, are you recommending VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink? we have customers with strict egress rules.
01:18 Priya: both supported, tradeoffs: peering is simpler but exposes routing; private link is more controlled and aligns with regulated customers. for the reference arch we'll include both patterns and a recommended default based on security posture.
01:30 Marta: for SOC2 customers we'll need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. do you have a pre-made section we can reuse?
01:37 Jordan: yes we have a partner security appendix. i will share a redwood security summary and the SOC2 scope doc. note that sometimes transcription and doc names get munged in notes, but i'll attach the actual PDFs.
01:49 Priya: also want to raise throttling and quota details — Marketplace listings often need clear SLO and quota fields. Redwood has token-based quotas and per-route configs; we'll include recommended defaults and an uplift for enterprise tiers.
02:05 Leah: about pricing — if we do joint SKU, who sets the price? and how do revisions work?
02:11 Jordan: typically partner sets the public price in the marketplace, we recommend a price sheet from us (cost per token + margin guide) and then partner chooses final list price. we'll propose a starter SKU mapping.
02:22 Samir: any perf numbers you can share for typical gen workloads? like 8k context chat, our customers worry about latency.
02:29 Priya: we'll include sample benchmarks. for hosted API median p50 is ~80-120ms for short prompts on our low-latency model; for dedicated with batching the numbers change but throughput is higher. note these are sample numbers, we'll run a joint benchmark on aurora infra.
02:45 Marta: can you run a bench on our staging region? we use aurora-eu-1 region.
02:50 Priya: yes, we can. need ssh/credentials for the staging cluster or we'll spin up a dedicated test node behind your VPC.
02:58 Jordan: action item — priya to produce a latency benchmark plan and the terraform snippets to deploy a small dedicated infra (notes: link to repo).
03:07 Samir: what about data retention and logs? customers ask about raw request retention. do you keep prompts?
03:13 Jordan: we support configurable retention. for marketplace and private deployments we can set retention to zero, or provide audit logs only, and integrate with your logging endpoints. we can also support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS/HSM for encryption at rest.
03:29 Marta: legal will need the partner agreement and the marketplace listing terms. who owns the customer contract?
03:34 Jordan: that is dependent on the listing mode — for direct listing via Redwood we own the customer contract; for a marketplace-managed offer AuroraCloud will be the primary contract holder. we'll put options in the partner playbook.
03:46 Priya: quick note on the reference arch: we'll include diagrams for three modes — hosted redirect, dedicated (reserved capacity), private (VPC/on-prem). each will show networking, key mgmt, and monitoring hooks (trace, token cost).
04:01 Leah: can you include a sample support contact flow? marketplace buyers ask how to triage incidents.
04:07 Jordan: yes, we'll add an escalation matrix. primarly Redwood handles inference runtime incidents, Aurora handles billing/support for marketplace-managed offers, and joint-run escalation for infra.
04:20 Marta: curious if we should do a joint one-pager and then a deeper RA doc for customers.
04:25 Jordan: suggested approach: one-pager for marketplace asset, RA as linked doc, and a github repo with terraform + sample deployment.
04:33 Samir: about certs — do you support mutual TLS for connections between aurora and the redwood endpoint?
04:38 Priya: we do, mTLS is supported for private links; for hosted API we rely on TLS + API keys, for private we can do mTLS or VPC peering.
04:47 Marta: ok good. next, timeline — we are trying to have a marketplace draft by end of the month and a pilot early june. is that realistic?
04:55 Jordan: yes, if we get artifacts this week and run the bench next week we can target an early june pilot.
05:02 Priya: i'll target terraform + bench plan out by 2026-05-20.
05:08 Jordan: i'll send the marketplace checklist and the partner security appendix by 2026-05-18.
05:14 Marta: legal will review the questionnaire and get back by 2026-05-22.
05:20 Leah: any blockers from our side? samir: networking might take a bit.
05:26 Samir: we may need a small network setup window, will coordinate with infra.
05:31 Jordan: great. recap: jordan shares checklist and SOC2 summary; priya provides RA diagrams, terraform, and bench plan; aurora returns questionnaire. prepare for pilot early june.
05:45 Jordan: thanks all, i'll follow up with calendar invites for a bench kick-off and share links to repo and docs.
05:51 Marta: thanks jordan, thanks team.
05:54 End of recording.
